analysis.evidence: מְתוּשֶׁלַח is the subject of וַיְחִי. The phrase אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת לֶמֶךְ marks the birth of Lamech as the starting point, and the following number gives the duration Methuselah lived after that birth, 782 years.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and an apocopated verb form.
analysis.sense: live for a stated length of time

analysis.evidence: מְתוּשֶׁלַח is the subject of וַיְחִי, “he lived.” The phrase אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת לֶמֶךְ, “after he fathered Lamech,” identifies him as Lamech’s father.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אַחֲרֵי governs the infinitive construct הוֹלִידוֹ in אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת לֶמֶךְ, “after he fathered Lamech.” The phrase marks the starting point of the 782 years Methuselah lived after that event.
analysis.morphology: Preposition in the plural construct form אַחֲרֵי, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת לֶמֶךְ, “after he fathered Lamech,” the suffix וֹ refers to Methuselah, and אֶת marks Lamech as the direct object.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive construct with a third-person masculine singular suffix marking the subject

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת לֶמֶךְ, “after he fathered Lamech,” אֶת marks the proper name לֶמֶךְ as the direct object of הוֹלִידוֹ.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for לֶמֶךְ with its derivation left open.
draft.definition: A masculine personal name borne here by the son of Methuselah.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:26 identifies Lamech by naming him as the son whom Methuselah fathered.

analysis.evidence: Methuselah is the subject of וַיְחִי, “he lived.” The phrase אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת לֶמֶךְ means “after he fathered Lamech.” The suffix on הוֹלִידוֹ refers to Methuselah, and לֶמֶךְ names his son.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun with no prefix or suffix. The preceding אֶת marks it as the direct object of הוֹלִידוֹ.

analysis.evidence: In שְׁתַּיִם וּשְׁמוֹנִים שָׁנָה, שְׁתַּיִם supplies the two in “eighty-two years.” Its feminine form agrees with שָׁנָה, “year.”
שְׁתַּיִם וּשְׁמוֹנִים שָׁנָה means “eighty-two years,” literally “two and eighty years.” The marked numeral supplies the tens in the count of years Methuselah lived after fathering Lamech.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, common gender, plural absolute, with prefixed conjunction וּ־ “and”.

analysis.evidence: In שְׁתַּיִם וּשְׁמוֹנִים שָׁנָה, the singular noun supplies the unit for ‘eighty-two years’. The following seven hundred years bring the total to 782 years that Methuselah lived after fathering Lamech.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: שְׁבַע counts מֵאוֹת ‘hundreds’. The conjunction adds these seven hundred years to the preceding eighty-two, giving 782 years.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ followed by שְׁבַע, the feminine construct form of the cardinal numeral.

analysis.evidence: In וּשְׁבַע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, שְׁבַע counts the hundreds and שָׁנָה supplies the unit, giving “and seven hundred years.”
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: In וּשְׁבַע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, “and seven hundred years,” the marked noun supplies the unit for the second part of the 782 years Methuselah lived after fathering Lamech.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Methuselah is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד, and בָּנִים וּבָנוֹת (“sons and daughters”) are its direct objects.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix
